harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: The requested LVM work completed successfully before reboot: /srv/data stayed mounted while growing from 1 GiB to 2.25 GiB, and its content remained intact. However, node1 did not restore SSH execution within five minutes after the mandatory reboot, so changed boot identity and post-restart persistence could not be verified.
actions_performed: Installed Ubuntu 7.10-compatible LVM2 without replacing the OS or kernel.
Created loop-backed PV /dev/loop0, VG vgdata, and LV lvdata.
Formatted lvdata as ext3 and mounted it at /srv/data.
Wrote an integrity file, then extended the mounted LV from 1 GiB to 2.25 GiB and resized ext3 online.
Configured boot-time device-mapper loading, loop attachment, VG activation, and mounting.
Captured a healthy restart baseline and initiated one acknowledged native reboot.
Polled node1 for approximately five minutes; SSH remained refused.

evidence.summary: vgdata/lvdata was created at 1 GiB and mounted read-write as ext3 at /srv/data.

evidence.requirement: Grow to at least 2 GB while remaining mounted
evidence.summary: Mount evidence appears before and after lvextend and online resize2fs. The final LV size was 2,411,724,800 bytes and filesystem size was 2,373,779,456 bytes.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed OS release and kernel
evidence.summary: Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic were retained; the release-native LVM2 2.02.26 package was used.
Boot-time dm_mod loading, rcS LVM activation/mounting, and the noauto fstab entry were configured. This is supporting configuration evidence only.

The healthy baseline and boot ID af07932d-bfd9-4ae7-aa6b-57a2c7a230b2 were captured; reboot acknowledgement returned; SSH then became unavailable and remained refused through the final poll. A changed boot ID and recovered storage could not be observed.

attempts.error: The requested LVM work completed successfully before reboot: /srv/data stayed mounted while growing from 1 GiB to 2.25 GiB, and its content remained intact. However, node1 did not restore SSH execution within five minutes after the mandatory reboot, so changed boot identity and post-restart persistence could not be verified.

diagnosis.summary: The online LVM operation succeeded before reboot: a mounted ext3 logical volume at /srv/data grew from 1 GiB to 2.25 GiB, remained mounted, and retained its test content. Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic were preserved. The final post-reboot state is unknown because SSH never returned; the evidence cannot distinguish a boot failure, an sshd failure, or unusually slow recovery.

evidence.finding: Before growth, /dev/mapper/vgdata-lvdata was mounted read-write at /srv/data with an LV size of 1,073,741,824 bytes.
lvextend and online resize2fs completed successfully, with mount checks succeeding before, between, and after those operations.
After growth, the LV was 2,411,724,800 bytes and the filesystem 2,373,779,456 bytes. integrity.txt retained the same SHA-256 and inode.
Immediately before reboot, the mount, LVM state, filesystem size, content hash, write access, and original kernel were healthy.

A custom rcS script, dm_mod entry, and noauto fstab entry were installed, but the script was only checked while the loop device, VG, and mount were already active; cold-start recovery was not demonstrated.
Reboot was scheduled and SSH subsequently remained refused. No changed boot ID or post-reboot storage state was captured.

likely_causes.cause: The custom loop-backed LVM startup path failed during cold boot because its detached/inactive recovery sequence was never tested before reboot.
The legacy guest rebooted but sshd failed to start or accept connections; connection refusal alone does not establish that the OS or LVM boot process failed.
The VM or platform failed to complete the reboot, independently of the LVM changes.
Installing LVM2 and regenerating the legacy initramfs introduced a boot regression.

next_attempt_guidance: Prefer a real spare block device or partition for the PV. Use a loop-backed sparse file only when no suitable block device exists.
Install only the release-native LVM2 package, record the OS and kernel, and verify free space before creating storage.
Capture before/after mount, LV byte size, filesystem byte size, and content hash exactly as this attempt did.

Before rebooting a loop-backed design, simulate a cold start: unmount /srv/data, deactivate the VG, detach the loop device, run the startup mechanism, then verify VG activation, mount, size, hash, and write access.
Use a late boot hook such as rc.local or a correctly ordered SysV service after local filesystems are available; keep the fstab entry noauto if the hook performs the mount.

If a restart is mandatory, capture boot ID before it and verify a changed boot ID, active LV, mounted filesystem, expected size, preserved hash, and write access afterward. If SSH does not return, report the cause as indeterminate rather than attributing it to LVM.
